item.title: Bernard Herrmann
item.description: Alfred Hitchcock wanted the shower scene in Psycho to play in silence.

item.title: Brian Eno
item.description: On Roxy Music’s first two records there is an instrument the credits can’t quite name: the rest of the band, fed through Brian Eno’s synthesizer and sent back out transformed.

item.title: Curtis Mayfield
item.description: The sound that made Curtis Mayfield unmistakable was built from a child’s shortcut.

item.title: Paul McCartney
item.description: Paul McCartney plays the bass like a second singer.

item.title: Ryuichi Sakamoto
item.description: As a Tokyo high schooler, Ryuichi Sakamoto rode a packed commuter train twenty minutes every morning and started counting the noise.

item.title: Ambient
item.description: For about a month in 1980, the Marine Air Terminal at LaGuardia played Ambient 1: Music for Airports as its actual terminal music, and the travelers complained: the record made them uneasy, and some said it sounded like funeral music.

item.title: Cinematic classical
item.description: In 1933 a Viennese émigré named Max Steiner laid continuous orchestral music under most of a film about a giant ape, and in doing so fixed the grammar of how movies would sound for the next ninety years.

item.title: Classical music
item.description: In 1829, the English organist Vincent Novello wrote in his diary of a Continental chapel that it was the place “I should come to every Sunday when I wished to hear classical music correctly and judiciously performed” — the first sentence the Oxford English Dictionary can find with the family’s name...

item.title: Modern classical
item.description: On December 22, 1894, in Paris, a flute opened Claude Debussy’s Prélude à l’après-midi d’un faune alone, sliding down to a tritone — the one interval the whole harmonic language had agreed must resolve — and letting it hang there, unaccompanied.

item.title: Spaghetti western
item.description: One evening during the 1968 Almería shoot, Sergio Leone filmed the scene where Claudia Cardinale’s character finds her new family laid out dead on tables, and he played Ennio Morricone’s music on set while the cameras rolled.
